meaning: Monthly active users: everyone who used Spotify in the month, free or paying.
A person paying for Spotify Premium.
A person using free Spotify; Spotify earns money from ads they hear.
All the money Spotify earns, before costs.
Spotify reports in euros; amounts here are converted to dollars at each year's average ECB exchange rate.
The % of revenue left after paying music royalties and delivery costs.
Profit after all running costs (staff, marketing, offices). Negative = loss.
Cash the business actually generated in the year after investments.
Average Revenue Per User: money earned from one user per month.
The % of subscribers who cancel each month. Spotify does not publish this, so we assume it.
Customer Acquisition Cost: marketing money spent to win one new subscriber (estimated here).
Lifetime Value: the profit one subscriber brings in before they cancel.
How many times a subscriber pays back what it cost to win them. 3x or more is usually healthy.
Months until a subscriber's profit covers the cost of winning them.
Simple divides marketing by growth only. Realistic also counts people won to replace those who cancelled, so it is lower and more believable.
